page: Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores using the ARMv9 architecture, powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The CPU configuration provides one thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or graphics processing units.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core performance, ranking in the top 25% for multi-core stress-ng tests and the top 10% for Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient, with cached small-block read bandwidth placing in the top 10% and uncached large-block read/write bandwidth in the top 25%. The processor excels in specialized tasks, achieving top-tier status in bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput. However, single-core stress-ng performance and LLM inference speeds for both 135M and 7B models remain in the average tier.

The instance offers high resource density and compute efficiency for ARM-native workloads, leveraging dedicated physical cores to avoid resource contention. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, and the absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy machine learning acceleration. Network bandwidth is rated at a baseline of 34 Gbps. This hardware profile is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, high-throughput web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded data processing.
